story.title: Fatal Amazon Cargo Plane Crash in Miami Under Investigation
story.summary: An Amazon cargo plane overran the runway at Miami International Airport, resulting in a crash that killed five people and injured five others. The aircraft struck two vehicles on the ground, including a cleaning crew van and an SUV. Investigators have recovered the flight data and cockpit voice recorders as the FAA and NTSB begin their investigation into the incident.

event_overview.title: About Fatal Amazon Cargo Plane Crash at Miami International Airport
event_overview.subject: Fatal Amazon Cargo Plane Crash at Miami International Airport
event_overview.summary: On September 6, 2026, a Boeing 767 cargo flight operated by 21 Air for Amazon overran a runway after arriving at Miami International Airport from San Juan, Puerto Rico. The aircraft struck ground vehicles and caught fire; five people were killed, and the crash is the subject of a federal safety investigation whose cause had not been determined as of September 8.

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: The accident occurred at about 2 p.m. local time on September 6, 2026, at Miami International Airport in Miami, Florida.

facts.label: Flight and aircraft
facts.value: FAA identified the flight as 21 Air Flight 7598, a Boeing 767-300 cargo aircraft that had departed Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport in San Juan, Puerto Rico.

facts.label: Casualties
facts.value: Five people were killed after the runway overrun struck ground vehicles; authorities also reported injuries. Reporting on September 8 said those killed were occupants of a van used by plane cleaners.

facts.label: Investigation
facts.value: The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating. Its process gathers evidence before issuing a final report that determines probable cause, so early facts should not be treated as conclusions about why the crash occurred.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the initial fatal crash and the next-day investigation developments, not the full recovery, airport-operations impacts, victim identifications, or the eventual NTSB findings.

explore_lenses.label: Why were ground workers so exposed?
explore_lenses.title: The deaths were outside the aircraft
explore_lenses.summary: The crash became a ground-safety disaster because the aircraft continued beyond Runway 30, through airport boundaries, and into areas used by workers and road traffic.

claims.text: NTSB Chair Jennifer Homendy said all five people killed were in the two vehicles struck by the aircraft, rather than aboard the cargo plane.
The plane hit a cleaning-company van carrying seven people inside the airport, then breached a perimeter fence and struck an SUV on Northwest 67th Avenue outside the airport.

This places runway-end protection, airport-perimeter design, and the routing of service and public vehicles among the safety questions that investigators may need to assess; no agency has yet assigned fault to any of those factors.

explore_lenses.label: What may have caused the runway overrun?
explore_lenses.title: The cause has not been determined
explore_lenses.summary: Federal authorities have confirmed an overrun after landing, but have not identified a mechanical, crew, airport, or weather cause. Weather conditions reported near the airport are context, not a finding of causation.

claims.text: The FAA says 21 Air Flight 7598, a Boeing 767-300 arriving from San Juan, overran the runway after landing at about 2 p.m. on September 6.
The NTSB’s case page identifies the event as a runway overrun during landing and lists the investigation as ongoing.
Thunderstorms and wind gusts up to 30 mph were recorded in the area at the time, but officials had not determined whether weather played a role.
The recovered flight-data and cockpit-voice recorders are evidence for investigators, not proof of a particular explanation before their analysis is released.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next for travelers and the probe?
explore_lenses.title: Reduced airport capacity and a long inquiry
explore_lenses.summary: Recovery work and evidence collection are still constraining MIA operations, while the NTSB process will proceed from factual findings to a later probable-cause report.

claims.text: Miami-Dade County said on September 7 that two of MIA’s four runways remained closed while investigators worked at the site.

As of September 8, the FAA’s airport-status page reported an active traffic-management program because of the disabled aircraft, with Miami-bound departures delayed by an average of 2 hours and 11 minutes.
Forecast: The NTSB says a preliminary report is typically available within weeks and that investigations generally take 12 to 24 months to complete, though timing varies with complexity.
Miami-Dade Mayor Daniella Levine Cava said the county will work with the NTSB and FAA and evaluate any safety recommendations produced by the review.

story_report.summary: An Amazon cargo plane, 21 Air Flight 7598, overran a runway after landing at Miami International Airport at about 2 p.m. on September 6 following a flight from San Juan. The aircraft struck two vehicles, killing five people and injuring five others. Flight-data and cockpit-voice recorders have been recovered as the Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board investigate the runway overrun, which also disrupted airport operations.

sections.heading: Victims and crash path
sections.body: NTSB Chair Jennifer Homendy said all five fatalities were occupants of the two vehicles hit by the aircraft, not people aboard the cargo plane. The plane first hit a cleaning-company van carrying seven people inside the airport, then broke through the perimeter fence and struck an SUV on Northwest 67th Avenue outside the airport.

sections.heading: Miami airport operations disrupted
sections.body: Miami-Dade County said on September 7 that two of Miami International Airport’s four runways remained closed while investigators worked at the crash site. As of September 8, the FAA reported an active traffic-management program because of the disabled aircraft, with Miami-bound departures delayed by an average of two hours and 11 minutes.

sections.heading: Federal investigation remains ongoing
sections.body: The NTSB identifies the event as a landing runway overrun and lists its investigation as ongoing. The agency says preliminary reports are typically available within weeks, while aviation investigations generally take 12 to 24 months, depending on complexity. Miami-Dade Mayor Daniella Levine Cava said the county will work with the NTSB and FAA and evaluate safety recommendations from the review.

unresolved.text: Officials had not determined whether thunderstorms and wind gusts of up to 30 mph contributed to the crash, and no preliminary probable-cause finding had been issued as of September 8, 2026.
Authorities have not said whether vehicle access or physical barriers contributed to the crash’s severity.
No date has been announced for full runway restoration or release of the NTSB preliminary report.

related_stories.title: Art Heist at Renoir Museum Leaves Two Paintings Missing
related_stories.summary: Thieves executed a heist at the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer, French Riviera, stealing four paintings. During their escape, they abandoned two of the artworks in the museum's gardens as police pursued them. Local authorities are investigating the incident, noting that the thieves appeared well-prepared and knowledgeable about the museum's layout.

related_stories.title: Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia Cause Injuries and Damage to Oil Facilities
related_stories.summary: The Iran-backed Houthi group launched a series of attacks on four cities in Saudi Arabia, injuring over 70 people and igniting fires at oil facilities. This escalation follows the collapse of a four-year truce and marks the Houthis' most significant assault in years. In response, Saudi Arabia has vowed to retaliate against the attackers.

related_stories.title: Attorney Requests Trump Pardon for Lindsay Clancy After Mistrial
related_stories.summary: Following a mistrial in her murder case, Lindsay Clancy's attorney has formally requested a pardon from Donald Trump. Clancy faces three murder charges related to the deaths of her three children. The prosecution now has the option to retry the case, negotiate a plea deal, or drop the charges altogether.

related_stories.title: Rescue Efforts Intensify in Nepal's Hydropower Tunnels After Devastating Floods
related_stories.summary: Rescue teams in Nepal are concentrating their efforts on three hydropower project tunnels where they believe many workers may be trapped. This comes two weeks after severe flooding resulted in over 1,300 fatalities and left approximately 5,000 individuals missing, including foreigners. The floods have affected both Nepal and the Tibet region of China.
